To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the membrane bioreactor produced a significant amount of organic matter that had a great impact on fouling formation and flux decline of nanofiltration membranes, and that the membrane characteristics played a significant role in flux decline of the membranes.

the MBR effluents contained large amounts of polysac-charide-like substances which had a great influence of fouling formation of NF membranes, while hydrophilic fraction was found as major constituent of the desorped NF membrane foulants and the flux decline rates of the membranes could be influenced by their characteristics (i.e. surface zeta potential, contact angle).

the membrane bioreactor produced large amounts of polysac-charide-like substances with strong fluorescence intensity at a specific excitation/emission wavelength and that the NF membrane fouling characteristics were governed by both the hydrophobic and the hydrophilic fractions of the effluent organic matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fouling characteristics of a hybrid system for municipal water reclamation.
the effects of changes in the characteristics of effluent OM by the MBR process on the fouling characteristics of NF membranes.
the effects of changes in organic matter characteristics on fouling characteristics, which will help us to understand the fouling mechanism of membrane bioreactors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fouling characteristics of a NF membrane were affected by both the characteristics of the MMR effluent organic matter and the characteristics of the membrane itself.
the fouling characteristics of NF membranes in the MBR and NF hybrid system were governed by both the membrane characteristics and characteristics of the effluent organic matters.
the MBR and NF hybrid system could be an alternative to conventional treatment processes for municipal wastewater reclaims.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MBR could be used as a promising pretreatment for the NF process in the hybrid system to improve fouling control and to enhance the performance of the NF membranes.
fouling formation of NF membranes was affected by the characteristics of the MBI effluents and the membrane characteristics.
the MBR and NF hybrid system could be a feasible alternative for municipal wastewater re-use.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MBR and NF hybrid system is capable of producing a high-quality reclaimed water with low fouling potential of the NF membranes, and the MBR is a very effective process to remove hydrophobic fractions of organic matter from municipal wastewater.
the NF membranes can be used to remove the foulants in the MBR effluent, which can reduce the fouling propensity of the NF membranes.
a hybrid system of MBR and NF could be an efficient approach to treat municipal wastewater for reclamation.
